board-view.name: board-radio
board-view.needs: an emulated board booted: node.boardview opens on a node pinned to a board image, but the panel, the tables and the console are all read from the running chip model, so a stopped node draws "this node is not running a board image". Booting one starts QEMU or Renode, which is a board probe rather than a screenshot - heavy enough that docs/development-machines.md says to run them one at a time
board-view.expect: the board's panel on the left, the Radio table with a verdict on every row, and the console along the bottom

board-view.name: board-wiring
board-view.needs: an emulated board booted: node.boardview opens on a node pinned to a board image, but the panel, the tables and the console are all read from the running chip model, so a stopped node draws "this node is not running a board image". Booting one starts QEMU or Renode, which is a board probe rather than a screenshot - heavy enough that docs/development-machines.md says to run them one at a time
board-view.expect: the board's panel on the left, the Wiring table with a verdict on every row, and the console along the bottom

board-view.name: board-decoded
board-view.what: The board view's console with the frames read out
board-view.needs: an emulated board booted: node.boardview opens on a node pinned to a board image, but the panel, the tables and the console are all read from the running chip model, so a stopped node draws "this node is not running a board image". Booting one starts QEMU or Renode, which is a board probe rather than a screenshot - heavy enough that docs/development-machines.md says to run them one at a time, and additionally a companion pinned to a board image: the decode tick is offered only where there is a framed protocol to decode, and no shipped fixture carries one on a board rather than a host build
board-view.expect: the decode tick is on and framed traffic reads as prose, with the plain boot log still beside it
